speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been suffering from chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and have there been any episodes of blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infectious Colitis (likely Campylobacter or other bacterial etiology) secondary to camping exposure, presenting with chronic symptoms due to incomplete resolution or post-infectious inflammatory bowel changes.
